score.note: Correctly distinguishes response-dependent and dynamic placeholder references from request-only expressions, with focused unit and end-to-end coverage.

The cancellation flow correctly keeps nested callers aligned with their children and wakes blocked runs after settlement, though the wake-up condition can emit unnecessarily for an already-completed run.

The parser and prefix overrides address the reported failure and key path cases, but forcing mnemonicPrefix off disregards the configured diff prefixes, and the visible tests mainly verify command arguments.
Matches the reference behavior for ZIP and squashfs, with focused coverage of link reads, suffix handling, and a hostile-archive escape attempt; explicit range/seek coverage is absent.
Implements the reference behavior, including direct ph() calls and request-only edge cases, with focused tests and no unrelated changes.

The recovery path is largely correct, but deferred closing delays reconnect until Gather ends, the extra engine/context resets may disrupt configured state, and the unrelated Gosmi test edit broadens scope; the package suite also failed.
Implements the reference fix with serialized reference-counted closes, double-close protection, abstract-socket safeguards, and focused coverage of the required lifecycle and race cases.
Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs symlink conventions, including safe suffix handling and an escape regression test; tests do not directly cover ranged or seek reads.
The parser and explicit prefixes address the core bug and most edge cases, but forcing a/ and b/ overrides mnemonicPrefix and stash diffs are not given parseable prefixes.
Implements the required close-and-reconnect recovery for failed gathers, but the package suite failed and the unrelated Gosmi test-path change weakens the patch.
Matches the reference fix and adds broad coverage across compaction paths, appender APIs, replay, cutoffs, and chunk reclamation; the extensive test scaffolding is somewhat complex.

Handles nested reusable-caller cancellation and stuck-run settlement with useful regression tests, though settling on every cancellation and emitting whenever no jobs changed are broader than necessary.
Correctly distinguishes response-dependent placeholders from request-only and dynamic expressions, with focused unit and retry-behavior coverage.
Implements the requested symlink convention consistently in ZIP and squashfs, with focused coverage for listing, reading, skipped links, suffix handling, and archive traversal safety.
Adds opt-in symlink support to both backends with range reads, lookup handling, collision defenses, and strong tests; the ZIP copy test lacks the Windows symlink-privilege skip used elsewhere.

The production changes implement exemplar-aware series retention and chunk reclamation, and the extensive tests cover both appenders, compaction paths, replay, cutoff behavior, and concurrent appends; the scope is relevant, though the test additions are substantial.
It preserves series identity after committed exemplars are replayable, but misses protection before commit and fails to clear the appender in ordinary GC; the added suite also fails.

The shared-FD refcount design addresses ordinary reuse, but the package suite fails and the patch does not explicitly guarantee net.ErrClosed on a second Close or derive the cleanup path from the bound socket address.

The implementation addresses prefix handling and diff-path resolution across the specified cases; command-argument tests cover the configuration changes, though focused parser edge-case tests are not apparent in the visible patch.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for reference counting, double-close, relisten races, immediate cleanup, and abstract sockets.

Nested callers remain cancelling until descendants settle, and settled runs trigger a concurrency recheck; the only minor concern is rechecking on every no-job cancellation even when the run status did not change.

The patch handles mnemonic and other prefixed paths and configures relevant Git commands to emit parseable prefixes, though forcing standard prefixes overrides the user’s mnemonic-prefix preference and the added tests mostly verify command arguments.
Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs symlink behavior, including safe names, lookup consistency, target reads, and focused regression and security tests.

The recovery path works for the usual unset-engine configuration, but restoring configured engine values can preserve stale state, and the package suite failed alongside an unrelated test-path change.
The SNMP recovery changes match the reference and are tested, but the unrelated MIB loader changes materially widen the patch.
Correctly identifies response-data placeholders, preserves request-only retry expressions, and adds focused tests for both forms and key edge cases.
Implements the reference lifecycle fix and adds focused coverage for cleanup, shared references, double closes, abstract sockets, and close/relisten races.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for final-close cleanup, shared references, double close, relisten races, and abstract sockets.
Implements the prefix configuration and robust header-path parsing across the relevant diff commands; the updated command tests are useful, though focused parser edge-case coverage is not evident.

The label-based retention snapshot covers common committed exemplars, but can miss accepted exemplars that are pending or evicted from the circular store while their WAL records remain replayable; the package suite also fails.

Addresses caller status aggregation and waking blocked runs after cancellation, with useful regression tests, though the caller test covers only one nesting level and the run emitter is invoked more broadly than necessary.

Correctly distinguishes response placeholders from request-only and dynamic expressions, with broad classifier tests and an end-to-end retry regression test; Placeholders returns its internal slice without cloning it.

Correctly keeps nested reusable callers aggregated through descendant cancellation and wakes concurrency reevaluation after a no-job run settlement; it can report unchanged callers as updates and emits on any no-job cancellation, slightly broader than necessary.

The nested-caller status propagation and concurrency wake-up are addressed with focused tests, though the wake-up condition is broader than necessary and the concurrency test does not exercise the full dispatch path.

The patch attempts to preserve exemplar-backed series across both GC paths and covers many scenarios, but it fails the package suite and all hidden PR tests, so the retention and chunk-release behavior is not reliable.
The reconnect and gather-error recovery address the root cause, but the patch resets extra SNMPv3 context/key state and includes unrelated test changes; the package suite also failed.
Implements the core reconnect and engine-state reset behavior with useful coverage, but the package suite failed and the unrelated Gosmi test change expands scope.

Implements opt-in symlink exposure for ZIP and squashfs with strong range, lookup, copy, and escape-prevention tests, though collisions between a link’s translated name and a real .rclonelink member remain ambiguous.
Correctly identifies response placeholders in both shorthand and direct ph calls while excluding request-only expressions; tests cover the key regressions but omit the dynamic-placeholder case.
Implements the ZIP and squashfs symlink conventions consistently, with focused tests for listing, reading, regular suffixed files, and a hostile archive escape.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for shared references, double closes, relisten races, and abstract sockets.

Implements symlink handling across ZIP and squashfs with useful range and escape tests, but LinkFilter.Allow can drop a regular `.rclonelink` member when a same-base file or directory exists, violating the explicit preservation requirement.
Implements the connection-close and SNMPv3 engine-state reset recovery correctly, with useful coverage, but includes an unrelated MIB test path change and the package suite failed.

The retention and chunk-release logic is otherwise thorough, but exemplar timestamps are recorded only during commit, leaving an accepted exemplar vulnerable to compaction while its appender is still open.

The parsing and patch-prefix changes address the reported cases, but forcing mnemonicPrefix=false changes user-visible diff formatting, and the visible tests mainly assert command arguments rather than parsing behavior.
The reference-counting design and focused tests are substantial, but the patch does not compile because it uses `io` and `fmt` without importing them.

Keeps reusable callers cancelling until their children settle, refreshes the run when a child changes without changing its caller, and re-emits settled runs; the main deviation is emitting on every empty cancellation result rather than only when the run status changes.
Implements the prefix-independent path parsing and forces parseable prefixes for Git-generated diffs, with focused command expectation updates and passing package and hidden tests.
It fixes mnemonic-prefix parsing and adds strong parser coverage, but does not explicitly clear diff.noprefix and omits the stash diff command, leaving the broader prefix guarantee incomplete.

The committed-exemplar paths and broad regression tests are solid, but GC can miss an exemplar staged in an uncommitted appender, and HasExemplarAtOrAfter reads the exemplar slice length before acquiring its read lock.

The storage-backed retention covers replayed exemplars and chunk release well, but compaction can still evict a series while an exemplar is staged in an appender because retention only sees committed storage.
